name: Banana peel
tip: Fruit peels break down into compost when kept with wet waste.

name: Vegetable scraps
tip: Raw and cooked vegetable scraps belong in the wet waste stream.

name: Tea leaves
tip: Loose tea leaves are biodegradable and can be composted.

name: Leftover rice
tip: Food leftovers decompose and should be separated from dry recyclables.

name: Egg shell
tip: Crushed egg shells are organic material suitable for composting.

name: Flowers
tip: Wilted flowers and leaves are compostable garden waste.

name: Plastic bottle
tip: Empty plastic bottles can be recycled when kept clean and dry.

name: Newspaper
tip: Clean, dry paper is recyclable; keep it away from wet waste.

name: Cardboard box
tip: Flatten clean cardboard so it can be collected for recycling.

name: Glass jar
tip: Empty glass jars belong with dry recyclables; handle broken glass carefully.

name: Metal can
tip: Rinse metal cans and put them with dry recyclables.

name: Milk packet
tip: Rinse and dry multilayer milk packets before sending them to a collection point.

name: Chips wrapper
tip: Keep flexible packaging clean and dry; check local collection options.

name: Old cloth
tip: Reusable textiles are dry waste and may be donated or collected separately.

name: Battery
tip: Batteries contain chemicals and metals; take them to a battery collection point.

name: CFL light
tip: CFLs contain mercury and must go to an authorised e-waste collection point.

name: Expired medicine
tip: Medicines can contaminate water; use a pharmacy or authorised take-back route.

name: Paint can
tip: Leftover paint and its container need a hazardous-waste collection route.

name: Wrapped sanitary waste
tip: Wrap sanitary waste securely and follow local authorised disposal guidance.

name: Old mobile phone
tip: Phones contain valuable and hazardous materials; use an e-waste take-back point.

name: Razor blade
tip: Enclose sharp blades safely and keep them out of household recycling.

name: Insecticide spray
tip: Chemical spray containers can be hazardous; follow the label and local collection rules.

name: Tetra pack
tip: Rinse cartons and check local facilities because composite packaging needs special recycling.

name: Greasy pizza box
tip: Grease-contaminated cardboard cannot be recycled with clean paper; compost if accepted locally.

name: Thermocol packaging
tip: Keep foam packaging dry and use a collection point that accepts expanded polystyrene.

name: Used tissue
tip: Soiled tissues are generally not recyclable with clean paper and should follow local wet-waste guidance.
